How-to and policies: Request a campus safety escort: 1. You can arrange an escort any time of day if you need to be accompanied from one campus location to another. \(page: “If you need to be accompanied from one point to another, you can arrange for a personal safety escort any time of day.”\) 2. Call Public Safety at 201- 684 -6666, or use a blue light telephone or other security phone box. \(page: “Call the Public Safety Department at 201- 684 -6666… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/campus-safety-escorts/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/campus-safety-escorts/)

How-to and policies: Get an immediate response to imminent danger: 1. If a student or the community is in imminent danger, contact Public Safety at \(201\) 684-6666. \(page: “If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/report-an-incident/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/report-an-incident/)

How-to and policies: Report a motor vehicle accident on campus: 1. Report every motor vehicle accident occurring on campus to Public Safety. \(page: “All motor vehicle accidents occurring on campus must be reported to the Public Safety Department.”\) 2. Know that Public Safety will notify Mahwah Police when someone is injured, significant property damage occurs in the officer’s judgment, or a vehicle owner requests police assistance. \(page: “Public Safety will n… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

How-to and policies: Take immediate steps after an assault: 1. Get to a safe place and arrange medical services as soon as possible. \(page: “Get to a safe place where you can make arrangements for medical services as soon as possible.”\) 2. Avoid washing, showering, using the bathroom, brushing your teeth, eating, smoking, or douching. \(page: “Do not wash your hands, shower, go to the bathroom, brush your teeth, eat, smoke, or douche.”\) 3. If possible, put … (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

How-to and policies: Report incidents: 1. Report incidents as a responsible member of the RCNJ community. \(page: “To be most effective as a partner of our campus safety efforts, we need your help by maintaining personal situational awareness and reporting incidents as a responsible member of the RCNJ community.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/director/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/director/)

How-to and policies: Request support from the Office of Title IX: 1. You may request support without participating in an investigation or filing charges. \(page: “Students do not need to participate in an investigation or file charges in order to request support from the Office of Title IX.”\) 2. Ask about support such as academic accommodations, housing changes, safety planning, transportation, or parking accommodations. \(page: “Support can include: Help in ident… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

How-to and policies: Report a missing student: 1. Reports may go to Public Safety, Residence Life, or another campus member; all reports must be referred immediately to Public Safety. \(page: “Reports of a missing student may be received by Public Safety, Residence Life, or other members of the campus. All such reports must be immediately referred to Public Safety”\) 2. Public Safety begins locating the student immediately and investigates the r… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/missing-student/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/missing-student/)

How-to and policies: Contacts: Public Safety (see https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/closing-of-college/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/closing-of-college/)

How-to and policies: II. Event Types/Examples/Protocols: Mass Email Campus Television Displays Official Social Media RCNJ Internet Home Page RCNJ Emergency Preparedness Site RCNJ Intranet Home Page b. Non-Emergency Notifications 1. Event Type: Weather/Utility-Related Disruptions Examples include but are not limited to events that may necessitate closures, cancellations, operational shifts, or delays, such as: snow or ice storms flooding power/utility ou… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/emergency-notification/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/emergency-notification/)

How-to and policies: Notify Public Safety using an emergency call box: 1. Use the button on an emergency call box to notify Public Safety. \(page: “In a click of the button, Public Safety will be notified.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/campus-safety/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/campus-safety/)

How-to and policies: Request access to a campus location: 1. Contact the ID room at publicsafety@ramapo.edu with your “R” number, full name, and the location where you are requesting access. \(page: “In order to get access to somewhere on campus, please contact the ID room at publicsafety@ramapo.edu with your “R” number, full name, and where you are requesting access to.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/id-cards/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/id-cards/)

How-to and policies: Know when the College issues an emergency notification: 1. The College immediately notifies the campus community after confirming a significant emergency or dangerous situation on campus that poses an immediate threat to community members’ health or safety. \(page: “The College is required to immediately notify the campus community upon confirmation of a significant emergency or dangerous situation occurring on the campus that involves an immediate thre… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/emergency-notification/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/emergency-notification/)

How-to and policies: Report an incident: 1. Call Public Safety at \(201\) 684-6666 or extension 6666 from an internal Ramapo College phone, or go to the Public Safety Department Office in C-wing, Room C-102. \(page: “Call the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666 \(or extension 6666 if using an internal Ramapo College phone\) or come to the Public Safety Department Office located on the ground floor of C-wing, Room C-102.”\) 2. Describe w… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-report/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-report/)

How-to and policies: Notify the appropriate office if federal agents attempt to enter a classroom: 1. If federal agents attempt to enter a classroom, they must present a judicial warrant under college protocol. \(page: “If federal agents attempt to enter a classroom, college protocol requires them to present a judicial warrant.”\) 2. Faculty should immediately notify Public Safety or the Office of General Counsel to verify the documents. \(page: “Faculty should notify the Public Safety Office or t… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/public-safety-frequently-asked-questions/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/public-safety-frequently-asked-questions/)

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
The available information does not say whether you have to attend a hearing.
- Office of Student Conduct: If this involved activating a fire alarm because of a policy violation such as using a candle, the listed first-violation outcome is a $150 fine and completion of a Fire Safety Reflection Sanction. [13]

**Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [24]

Sources: [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/recommended-judicial-sanctions/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
**Student Accounts**
Log into RCNJ Experience ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)) Locate the Student Account Info card Click on Bill & Payment Suite Click on Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu You must enroll in a Two-Step Verification Process (If previously completed, skip this step) Click on the Security Settings tab in My Profile Select a method to receive a passcode (text message, email or Google Authentication) Click the Send Code button Enter the passcode and click the Verify button Click on the Payment Profile tab in My Profile Edit existing saved Payment Method or Create New Payment Method When either editing an existing payment method or creating a new one, click on check box in the Refund Option section to designate this payment method as the refund account for direct deposit. [1]
Should a Title IV financial aid overpayment result in a credit balance of $1.00 or greater, a refund will be issued. Credit balances from non-Title IV financial aid are subject to a $5.00 threshold. question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

**Housing & Residence Life**
Residents interested in requesting a room change must submit a Room Change Request Form during the open room change period. More information about the room change process, including important dates and instructions, is available here ([https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/)). [1]
Students interested in a room change for the Spring 2027 semester must submit a room change request form via the Room Change Process Website. ([https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/)) Room change request forms are due by November 24, 2026 at 11:59pm. Requests after this date will not be accepted. [4]
Before submitting a request, we recommend: Reviewing the full process on the webpage Checking the Residence Life Events & Important Dates ([https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/)) calendar to understand how a room change might affect you Room changes are not guaranteed. Requests depend on available space and other factors, and final decisions are made by the professional Residence Life staff. return to top. [5]

**Ombuds Office**
Listens to and discuss questions, concerns, and complaints Helps evaluate various options to address concerns Answers questions or help find others who can Explains College policies and procedures Facilitates communication between people Advises individuals about steps to resolve problems informally Advises individuals about formal and administrative options Mediates disputes to seek “win-win” resolution of problems Makes appropriate referrals when informal options don’t work Points out patterns of problems/complaints to administrators. [12]
Mediation is a process in which an impartial third party assists disputants in finding a mutually acceptable solution to their dispute. Mediation is both voluntary and confidential. [15]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [22]
- **Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/ombuds/ombuds/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/ombuds/services/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Missed 3 classes last week because I was in the hospital. How do I get my professors to excuse the absences, is there an office that sends a note or something?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

1. Health Promotion says to communicate directly with your professors about missing classes. [1]
2. Admissions says to speak with your instructors about making up missed work; course attendance is determined by the instructor. [2]
3. Office of Specialized Services says to account for your absence to your instructors and contact them to find out if and when work may be made up. [14]
The information provided does not identify an office that sends an excuse note.

- **Health Promotion**: Email: studentwellness@ramapo.edu. Wellness Is Now office: E-211A. [35]
- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [35]

These offices can help:
- **Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [36]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [36]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/health-promotion/immune-disease-tips/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/faqs/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [36](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can alumni still use career services and the library after graduating

body.answer:
Yes, alumni can use career services and some library services after graduating. The Office of Alumni Relations says alumni can access the Cahill Career Center’s services on the Ramapo campus, including help with job searches, resume updates and interviewing skills. [2] Alumni can use the library’s online services, borrow books and access the Learning Commons. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/benefits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/benefits/)

Alumni do not have off campus access.

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
**Student Accounts**
Spring 2027 Payment Plan Ramapo College offers two monthly payment plan options for the Spring semester beginning November 16, 2026, a four-month and a five-month plan. The Ramapo Tuition Payment Plan (RTPP) for Spring requires a $60 set-up fee and a 20% down payment for the five-month plan, and a 25% down payment for the four-month plan. Both are due at the time of enrollment. Students must enroll in the plan prior to the posted payment deadline for the semester and enrollment must be done online by logging into RCNJ Experience. The terms of the plan are as follows: Enrollment and the down payment for the plan is due by the appropriate payment deadline, with additional payments due on the 15th of each month thereafter. You must pay your down payment along with your non-refundable $60 set-up fee at the time of enrollment. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: refund

body.answer:
Student Accounts says:
- A Title IV financial aid overpayment that creates a credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; non-Title IV financial aid credit balances have a $5.00 threshold. [5]
- Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address. Checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up in the Office of Student Accounts. [5]
- If entitled to a fall-term refund, you may ask to apply it to the spring term by emailing studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Spring refund proceeds cannot be applied to the following fall term. [5]
- Free electronic refunds deposit directly into a checking or savings account: Sign up for Electronic Refunds ([https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/)) or Learn More About Electronic Refunds ([https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/)). [5]
- The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [5]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [11]

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [23]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

**Financial Aid**
If you drop below full-time status your financial aid will be adjusted. Federal aid requires you to be enrolled in 6 credits in a semester. If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. If you have state aid that is subject to being canceled and institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away. [2]
In order to receive financial aid, students must maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress add Sap policy link [https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/#s1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/#s1) ([https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/#s1k](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/#s1k)). [3]
Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) for continued financial aid eligibility is reviewed every year after the conclusion of the spring semester. Students not making financial aid SAP are no longer eligible for financial aid (this includes federal and state grants and scholarships, federal work-study and federal student loans) but, may request and receive certain alternative loans to attend Ramapo College. Quantitative Measure At the time of the SAP review, students’ academic records must show they are completing a minimum of 67% of credits attempted toward graduation requirements. [4]

**Office of the Provost**
Dropping or withdrawing from a course may affect issues concerning, but not limited to, financial aid eligibility, satisfactory progress towards graduation, athletic compliance, housing status, and involvement in campus activities and functions. [6]

**Registrar**
Your Name (First and Last) Ramapo ID Number (aka R#) CRN (Course Identification Number) Subject (Example: INTD) Course Number (Example 100) Section Number (Example 01) Title of the Course A student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline. [13]

question: is my 1098-T available yet? need it for taxes and cant find where to get it. also how do i get a copy of last years

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

It depends: Student Accounts provides Form 1098-T each year on or before January 31, but the facts don’t confirm whether this year’s form is already available. [2] It is an IRS tax form that can help students and families determine eligibility for the Hope Scholarship or Lifetime Learning Tax Credit; it applies to students who incurred qualified tuition and related expenses and paid corresponding payments during the current tax year. [1] The form reports the prior tax year, January 1 through December 31, not the academic year. [3]

Student Accounts: Forms are not mailed; eligible students can view and print them in the Bill and Payment Suite. [4][5]

1. Log into RCNJ Experience ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)). [2]
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click the Bill & Payment Suite link. [2]
3. Click the My Account tab at the top of the screen and select Statements. [2]
4. Click the 1098-T Tax Statements tab, then click View for the appropriate tax year. A printable or savable PDF will generate. [2]

To receive a printed copy for the current tax year only, complete the Revocation of Electronic 1098T form ([https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/wp-content/uploads/sites/147/2026/02/Revocation-of-Electronic-1098T_2026.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/wp-content/uploads/sites/147/2026/02/Revocation-of-Electronic-1098T_2026.pdf)) and submit it to the Office of Student Accounts. [2] The form will be printed within 5-7 business days and mailed to the home address on file with the Registrar’s Office. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [24]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/taxinfo/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/taxinfo/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/taxinfo/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/forms/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
Orientation Programs:
1. All students must apply for a permit online. [7]
2. Click the RCNJ Parking Permits ([https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/)) link and follow the Parking Permit Application Instructions. [7]
3. To complete the application, log on directly to the RCNJ Parking Permits ([https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/)) website, enter Permit Type and click Continue. [7]
4. Complete the Contact Information page, click Save/Update Person, then click Continue. [7]
5. Enter Vehicle Information and click Continue. [7]
6. Review your request and click Continue. [7]
7. Print or save the Registration Filed page, which includes your registration request number; this serves as your application verification. [7]
8. Commuter students receive a rearview mirror hang tag to register two vehicles on one permit at no additional fee. [7]
The information provided does not specify where commuters may park.

**Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [22]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm a commuter student and I have a 3 hour gap between classes. Is there somewhere on campus I can study or hang out, like a commuter lounge, and is there a way to store my stuff?

body.answer:
Yes, there is a place to relax between classes, and you can rent a locker to store your things. [3][5]

- Center for Student Involvement: J. Lee’s is the unofficial Commuter Lounge where students can kick back and relax before or after classes. [3]
- Center for Student Involvement: It features video games, a pool table, a ping pong table, and FREE POPCORN! [3]
- Center for Student Involvement: It is in the student center on the second floor between the Student Government office and the Black Student Union office. [3]
- Center for Student Involvement: Students may come to the Student Center Office to rent small or medium lockers for use during the academic semesters. [5]
- Center for Student Involvement: The lockers are in the second-floor stairwell area, between B and C buildings. [5]
- Center for Student Involvement: The rental fee is $10.00 for the semester and $20.00 for the academic year. [5]
- Center for Student Involvement: A key is issued with payment and must be returned at the end of the semester. [5]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [25]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/commuter-affairs/involvement-frequently-asked-questions/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: at any given time. Guests may not move from host to host to stay on-campus more than three (3) nights.
However, residents have the right to opt-out of this automatic Guest Registration by contacting their Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract.
As with any roommate/suitemate/apartment contract, if someone violates the terms of the contract, staff in the hall/area office must receive a formal complaint before they can act upon it.

It is the responsibility of roommates/suitemates to alert the host of the guest of any issues or concerns they may have concerning any guests or the amount of guests entering their room/suite/apartment.
It is recommended that students have open conversations with roommates/suitemates about guest expectations.

Residents who are aware of a person(s) living on-campus without authorization or who is violating the Guest Policy, should notify their residence hall office staff as soon as possible.

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [23]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

**Office of the Provost**
A student who decides to withdraw from a course after the 50% refund period (but no later than the last day to withdraw from a course, as indicated on the academic calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/))) may do so by accessing a withdrawal form online, completing a course withdrawal form in the Office of the Registrar, or, withdrawing online through Web Self Service. Once the withdrawal form is processed by the Office of the Registrar, the student will receive a W for the withdrawn course, and both student and instructor of record will receive notification that the student has withdrawn from the course. [1]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [24]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: A student who decides to withdraw from a course after the 50% refund period (but no later than the last day to withdraw from a course, as indicated on the academic calendar (https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) may do so by accessing a withdrawal form online, completing a course withdrawal form in the Office of the Registrar, or, withdrawing online through Web Self Service.

Once the withdrawal form is processed by the Office of the Registrar, the student will receive a W for the withdrawn course, and both student and instructor of record will receive notification that the student has withdrawn from the course.

question: something fell off the ceiling in my bathroom and theres a leak. who do I call at night, public safety or facilities?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-7432; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Hours: Monday to Sunday: 24 hours. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: The Public Safety Department is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu Parking Permits: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Get an immediate response to imminent danger: 1. If a student or the community is in imminent danger, contact Public Safety at \(201\) 684-6666. \(page: “If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/report-an-incident/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-6666; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Facilities Management**

Phones: (201) 684-7660; (201) 684-7670 (Receiving / Storeroom) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

**Housing & Residence Life**

Contact the right office for a facilities emergency: 1. Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM: call Facilities at 201-684-7660. \(page: “Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM \| The Office of Facilities \([https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)\) \| 201-684-7660”\) 2. After 4:30 PM and on weekends: call Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “After 4:30 PM & Weekends \| Public Safety \| 201-684-6666”\) 3. 8:00 PM–12:00 midnight: contact the RA Hall Office. \(page: “8:00 PM–12:00 Midni… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

Get immediate help with an emergency when the hall/area office is closed: 1. Call Public Safety at 201-684-6666 for immediate emergency assistance when the office is closed. \(page: “If the office is closed and you need immediate assistance for an emergency, you may call Public Safety at 201-684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/facilities-services/)

This office can help:
**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
**Student Accounts**
Log into RCNJ Experience ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)) Locate the Student Account Info card Click on Bill & Payment Suite Click on Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu You must enroll in a Two-Step Verification Process (If previously completed, skip this step) Click on the Security Settings tab in My Profile Select a method to receive a passcode (text message, email or Google Authentication) Click the Send Code button Enter the passcode and click the Verify button Click on the Payment Profile tab in My Profile Edit existing saved Payment Method or Create New Payment Method When either editing an existing payment method or creating a new one, click on check box in the Refund Option section to designate this payment method as the refund account for direct deposit. [1]
Should a Title IV financial aid overpayment result in a credit balance of $1.00 or greater, a refund will be issued. Credit balances from non-Title IV financial aid are subject to a $5.00 threshold. Unless otherwise specified by the student, the College will issue a paper check. Paper Check Refund – Checks will be mailed to the student’s billing/permanent address. Spring refund proceeds cannot be applied to the following fall term Electronic/Direct Deposit Refund – This free electronic refund service will deposit refunds directly into a student’s checking or savings account Sign up for Electronic Refunds ([https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/)) Learn More About Electronic Refunds ([https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/)) The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life:
1. Once housing assignments have been made, the Office of Residence Life is unable to accommodate room change requests prior to the start of the semester. [1]
2. Submit a Room Change Request Form during the open room change period. [2]
3. Visit the Room Change Process webpage ([https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/)) for important dates and instructions. [3]
4. The Room Change Process webpage ([https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/)) has step-by-step details and a link to the digital Room Change Request Form, available during active room change periods. [4][5]
5. Before submitting, review the full process on the webpage and check the Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/)) to understand how a room change might affect you. Room changes are not guaranteed. [6]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [22]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can alumni still use career services and the library after graduating

body.answer:
Yes. The Office of Alumni Relations says alumni can use the library’s online services, borrow books, and access the Learning Commons.[1] Alumni can also use the Cahill Career Center’s services on the Ramapo campus, including help with job searches, resume updates, and interviewing skills.[2]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/benefits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/benefits/)

pageFacts.question: can alumni still use career services and the library after graduating

facts.says: Utilize the online services of the library.
Book borrowing is also available to alumni.
Visit the library (https://www.ramapo.edu/library/) for more information, or download the Library Benefits (https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/wp-content/uploads/sites/195/2013/08/Library-Benefits.doc).
Alumni also have access to the Learning Commons.
Alumni are able to access the services of the Cahill Career Center (https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/) on the Ramapo campus.
Get help with job searches, resume updates, interviewing skills and more.
For additional information, please reach out to the Cahill Career Center at (201) 684-7444 or careercenter@ramapo.edu (mailto:careercenter@ramapo.edu).
Alumni do not have off campus access.

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
1. On-Campus Employment for Students: Federal work-study and student aide positions are posted on Handshake, ramapo.joinhandshake.com ([http://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/](http://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/)); all available Student Assistant positions are posted at [https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/](https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/). [12][15]
2. Register on Handshake to view open positions, then search using the keyword ‘RCNJ’. [15]
3. Follow each posting’s application instructions and contact its listed supervisor; you can apply directly to the hiring unit. [15][14]
4. If offered a position and you accept, discuss with the supervisor the job description and skill compatibility, start date, weekly hours (not conflicting with classes), schedule variations (mid-terms, exams, breaks), conduct and dress, salary, responsibility for college facilities and equipment, confidentiality, sign-in/out procedures (timekeeping), punctuality and attendance. You and the supervisor sign an employment form with beginning work date, salary, etc. Return all required paperwork (New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form) to the Student Assistant Program Office in Room D-119. [14]

**On-Campus Employment for Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7654. Email: sap@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [23]

Sources: [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/faqs/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/policies-and-procedures/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
